The weakest-link state requires genuinely unshielded tax exhaustion before cost shocks receive substantial weight, without introducing a binary subsample gate.

EXPECTED_SIGN: negative

Scaling cash by smoothed cost of goods sold creates an operating-runway measure rather than another cash-to-assets ratio, while industry ranks reduce structural sector differences.

NAME: Asset Renewal During Tax Exhaustion
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(dp, at), 3), 1), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(txt, at), 5))))

EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The strong unshielded-tax result implies that low depreciation makes tax exhaustion particularly adverse; this signal tests whether a rising depreciation base marks the opposite economic transition toward renewed productive capacity and greater noncash tax shields. Using a signed depreciation trend avoids merely sorting on static capital intensity.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
